examples.explanation: Identical thioanhydride linkages are named with the multiplicative prefix bis-.
The identical linkages use bis(thioanhydride) after the acetic and methanedisulfonic components.
O is senior to S, so the oxygen anhydride is the basis and the other linkage is named substitutively.
The figure illustrates a senior anhydride basis with three other linkages expressed as tris(thioanhydride).
The example shows an oxygen anhydride used as the senior basis while the sulfur linkage is substitutive.
The example shows another substitutive name for a non-senior sulfur anhydride linkage.
A thioacyl carbonyl is named using the thiocarboxylic acid and thioacyl treatment described for dianhydrides.
Both thioic carbonyl replacements are represented in the dianhydride name.
The example applies the thioacyl treatment to a sulfur-containing cyclic-anhydride analogue.
The example extends the anhydride treatment to a longer dianhydride containing a thioacyl linkage.
The preferred heterocyclic pseudoketone name is shown with systematic and retained acid-derived alternatives.
The methyl-substituted example uses the same two naming methods.
The retained name maleic anhydride is paired with the preferred heterocyclic pseudoketone name.
The bromo-substituted example illustrates both the preferred and retained-name forms.
The example shows the preferred heterocyclic pseudoketone name and the systematic and retained alternatives.

examples.explanation: The fused-ring example illustrates the preferred heterocyclic pseudoketone method for a dibasic acid anhydride.

The cyclic dianhydride example illustrates both allowed naming methods.
The second cyclic dianhydride example applies the same preferred heterocyclic method.
The table records the three numbering diagrams, the preferred PIN associated with (I), the not-name associated with (II), and the acid-derived name associated with (III).
Both the preferred heterocyclic pseudoketone names and the thioanhydride class-term names are shown.
The example demonstrates a chalcogen cyclic anhydride named as a heterocyclic pseudoketone.
